newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen 50-75 cts down,Brent 5-10 cts down.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen 50-75 cts down,Brent 5-10 cts down.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures are expected to open moderately weaker on Monday, extending the lethargic mood which has gripped the market since Tuesday's sharp slide, dealers said.
June gas oil, which settled Friday at $172.50 a tonne, should begin trading 50 to 75 cents a tonne weaker, while July Brent should come in 5-10 cents down on its close of $19.40 a barrel.
July Brent dropped 78 cents last Tuesday to $19.22 a barrel as smaller investment funds liquidated positions but some brokers said the market was still looking "top-heavy".
"We still need a shake-out. This market will remain pretty dull until it comes lower again," said a broker.
July Brent was firmly established in a 50-cent range between $19.10 and $19.60 a barrel, brokers said.
Even the expected renewal later this week of the U.N. accord with Iraq allowing oil sales in exchange for humanitarian imports was unlikely to shake the market out of its torpor.
"That's already been taken into account," said a broker.
U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan is due to submit his recommendation on the pact's renewal to the Security Council later on Monday.
Iraq completed on Friday the export of 120 million barrels of crude oil, raising $2 billion during the first six months of the U.N. deal which came into effect on December 10 last year.
Dealers said gas oil could benefit from the return of key German players following a holiday last Thursday and from a seasonal upturn in French demand.
"This is usually the time of year when French end users start to restock," said a broker.
Last week's low of $171.75 a tonne would provide front-line support for June gas oil, he said.
